analysis.title: The AI Sell-Off: Which stocks are being over punished? Part 2 - The more complete shopping list across the AI value chain
key_insights: Across 66 stocks in 9 AI value chain sectors, data center exposure explains about 40-45% of forward multiple derating. Regression R-squared is 0.45 on FY1 OP share and 0.36 on OP growth share, so the reset is market-wide.

Each additional 10%pts of data center OP exposure is associated with about 4.7%pts more forward-multiple compression. The fitted line runs from roughly -16% at zero exposure to roughly -63% at 100% exposure.
Bernstein argues the sell-off conflates AI exposure with hyperscaler and neocloud construction exposure. Enterprise on-prem AI and consumer AI are less tied to new campus construction.
Post-election pipeline work suggests limited capacity impact. Credible pipeline in restrictive jurisdictions rose from 78GW to 105GW, about 17GW is at risk, and the realistic nationwide loss is 2-4%.

Nvidia CEO transition (Jensen Huang departure) raises questions on who underwrites new neocloud capacity. Nvidia has reportedly extended $164.5B of commitments and guarantees, and existing contractual obligations are expected to be honored. Unsigned deals such as Nscale and a $500B+ financing platform are more at risk.

Hyperscaler channel checks (n=5) show permitted or funded projects proceeding, but a possible air pocket in cooling and power equipment orders through 4Q26/1Q27. Deferred orders could return by mid/2H27. IT hardware read-across is lagged.

Component supply (GPUs, CPUs, memory, storage, optics) is as binding as site readiness, so isolated site delays should shift timing rather than destroy hardware demand. SMCI recovered about $2.3B of slipped revenue and IREN's Microsoft delay was 1-2 months.

IT hardware, memory and storage: Server OEMs and Memory are the most over-punished, with multiples compressed 30-45%pts more than exposure implies. STX, WDC and DELL are modestly over-punished by 10-15%pts. SNDK and memory exposure may be understated because AI-driven pricing could make OP growth exposure close to 100%.

DELL is the preferred AI infrastructure name. Neocloud servers are 26.9% of FY27 revenue but only 11.7% of OP. The $95bn AI server backlog is mostly noncancelable and traditional server orders rose 122% YoY in fiscal 2Q27. DELL is preferred over HPE and SMCI.
SMCI screens as the most over-punished, with forward P/E down about 78% versus a fitted -38%, but China smuggling case risk, execution and dilution keep it Market-Perform.
STX and WDC are supported by an early-innings HDD pricing upcycle. STX is preferred for HAMR leadership and WDC carries more technology risk.

SNDK is over-punished on multiples, though the market may be underestimating LTA protections and SLC/HBF wafer intensity. If HBF at 6.5x trade ratio were 5% of NAND bits, it would need about 28% more wafers.

AAPL is the clearest safe haven, trading at 35.8x forward P/E, 19% above its 3-year average. Bernstein sees near-term pressure from Dec-quarter gross margin guidance of 45-46% and Services growth of 8-9%, and prefers opportunistic entry.
Networking has held up best. ANET, CSCO and GLW are under-punished. Ciena is the most over-punished relative to scale-across exposure, which benefits from power and land constraints.

COHR and LITE are fairly punished but face nonlinear downside if indium phosphide flips from undersupply to oversupply. A slower Nvidia roadmap would hurt CPO adoption and the laser supply chain, and benefit Celestica and possibly Arista.

US semis: OP growth explains derating better than OP exposure (R-squared 0.23/0.38). AVGO is the top pick, at about 15x CY27 and 9x CY28 EPS, with a resilient VMware business and frontier-lab customers. NVDA is seen as most affected by data center slowdowns.

Japan/EU semis: Advantest (19x forward, below -2SD) and Kokusai (14x forward) are over-punished. Ibiden screens under-punished only because its 3-year average is inflated. ASML is at about 20x 2027 P/E.

Emerging AI infra: RIOT ($38Bn contracts, about 50% discount to contract value) and WULF ($27Bn, about 30% discount) look over-punished. The group trades below $3Mn EV/MW and IREN is down more than 70% in two months.

EQIX and DLR are seen as justifiably resilient and arguably over-discounted. EQIX trades at 20.6x forward AFFO, 6% below its 3-year average, and DLR at 20.2x, about 17% below. CRWV remains Underperform because it is under-punished at 100% exposure.

Electrical equipment: FPS and LGN are the most over-punished by 20-30%pts. Multis such as VRT and JCI screen under-punished mainly on idiosyncratic outperformance. NVT is liked, though an orders air pocket is possible.
Energy: GEV screens over-punished at about 15% data center OP exposure and is down 35.4% from its 7/6/26 high of $1,195.94. BE is under-punished but fairly punished, with Market-Perform maintained.

earnings_insights: DELL reported fiscal 2Q27 traditional server orders +122% YoY, and the AI server backlog is $95bn per management.
DELL FY27 estimates (Bernstein): neocloud AI servers are about 26.9% of revenue, 11.7% of OP and 16.1% of OP growth from FY26A.
SMCI recent quarter included about $2.3B of revenue recovered from previously slipped deployments, with forward P/E now 3.2x.

IREN reported last week that its Microsoft deployment slipped 1-2 months. It lowered its fiscal 2027 capex plan by $7.5B on tighter financing, and its $4Bn cloud ARR target for early 2027E is fully funded.
EQIX reported 3Q26 as its fourth straight quarter of double-digit normalized MRR growth and raised full-year guidance for a third consecutive quarter.
DLR reported record 3Q26 leasing and raised its full-year core FFO outlook.
AAPL December-quarter gross margin guidance of 45-46% was below expectations, with Services growth expected to moderate to 8-9%.

Bernstein ticker table adjusted EPS (2026E / 2027E estimates): DELL $25.88 / $29.63, AVGO $11.64 / $18.63, NVDA $9.64 / $17.18, STX $43.11 / $72.97, WDC $27.30 / $45.26, SNDK $29.06 / $36.54, with some names on reported rather than adjusted EPS per the table footnotes.
VRT had a very strong 3Q and ANET a massive beat and raise in its most recent quarter, per Bernstein.
crypto_views: Bitcoin miners converting to AI data centers (RIOT, CORZ, CIFR, WULF, IREN, CLSK) are covered. RIOT's contracts ramp in 2028E so mining economics still drive FY27E operating growth, and CLSK runs 50 EH/s of mining.
Emerging AI infra developers signed $132Bn of AI deals in 24 months, about 85% colocation, and the group trades below $3Mn EV/MW with a 26% median discount to contracted NOI at 8-9% cap rates.

risk_factors: Greenfield data center order pause extending beyond early 2027 could create a gap in hardware orders tied to 2028+ capacity.
Nvidia interim leadership may be more cautious on new credit guarantees, raising neocloud cost of capital.
Tightening AI financing markets and neocloud scrutiny.
Possible near-term orders air pocket in cooling and electrical equipment through 4Q26/1Q27.
InP oversupply and slower Nvidia roadmap or CPO adoption risk for COHR and LITE.
NAND capacity additions in 2028-29 could normalize pricing and earnings abruptly for SNDK.
The regression is a starting point rather than a verdict, and small channel check sample (n=5).
SMCI China overhang and equity dilution.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots forward P/E change vs 3-year average against data center share of FY1 OP for the universe, with fitted line y = -0.4719x - 0.1593 and R-squared 0.4474.
Exhibit 2 plots the same against data center share of FY1 OP growth, fitted line y = -0.3984x - 0.1506 and R-squared 0.3589.
Exhibits 3 and 4 show the hardware, memory and networking subset with R-squared of 0.58 and 0.49 and slopes of -0.74 and -0.62.
Exhibits 7 and 8 show semis and semicap with R-squared of 0.23 and 0.38.
Exhibits 11 and 12 show data center infrastructure excluding DLR, CIFR, CORZ and RIOT, with R-squared of 0.64 and 0.65.
vol_and_positioning: Emerging AI infra stocks have a median drawdown of about 35% over two months, and IREN is down more than 70%.
Semicap front-end names trade around -1SD of the 3-year average multiple and back-end around -2SD. Screen and Kokusai peak-to-trough drawdowns are about 64% and 63%.
SMCI forward P/E has fallen about 78% from its 3-year average and SNDK about 76%, the largest derating outliers in the universe.
geopolitical: Concern that Chinese transceivers could be banned, which could trigger retaliation, weighs on optical names COHR and LITE.
SMCI China ties and a prior smuggling case in which two employees and one contractor were indicted could resurface after the Jensen Huang revelations.
Post-midterm election state-level data center restrictions in Texas, Georgia and Ohio are driving construction and permitting uncertainty.

tension_points.bull_case: Evidence points to project-level delays and higher costs rather than demand destruction. Component supply is binding, and permitted or funded builds through 2027 and early 2028 are largely locked in.
tension_points.bear_case: Greenfield capacity is paused awaiting policy clarity, which could cause an air pocket in power and cooling orders. Nvidia leadership change could tighten neocloud financing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A pause in greenfield commitments extending beyond early 2027, which would show up as a hardware order gap tied to 2028+ capacity.

tension_points.bull_case: InP bottlenecks have driven up laser prices and CPO on Rubin Ultra is a demand catalyst, with both stocks rated Outperform.
tension_points.bear_case: A data center slowing or slower Nvidia roadmap could flip InP from undersupply to oversupply, with disproportionate impact on Lumentum.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Push out in data center spend or slower Nvidia CPO adoption.

theme_stances.key_argument: Valuations have reset despite limited evidence of widespread demand destruction, creating selective buying opportunities in names with less hyperscaler and neocloud exposure than headline AI revenue implies.
